newsitem.title: USA: Select sees matching Q2, year estimates.
newsitem.headline: Select sees matching Q2, year estimates.

text.p: Select Appointments (Holdings) Plc said on Tuesday that it expects its earnings per ADR to match analysts' consensus estimate of $0.13 for the second quarter and $0.60 for full-year 1997.
Select reported first-quarter net income per share of $0.11, matching the consensus estimate and up from $0.07 for the same period a year ago.

"I think the rest of 1997 will be a progression from the first quarter," with the company meeting analysts' expectations of net income per ADR of $0.18 in both the third and fourth quarters, Select Chairman Tony Martin said in an interview.
The London-based company provides temporary and contract staffing services in 21 countries. Its biggest single market is North America, where sales were up 77 percent during the first quarter.
Martin said the company has grown both internally and through acquisitions, and he is confident these trends will continue.
"We'll probably be making some further acquisition this year," he said. "There are some things in Europe in the pipeline."

Martin said 1.8 percent of American workers are temporary or contract workers, up from 1.0 percent five years ago. He predicted that his type of service increasingly will appeal to employers seeking a flexible workforce so they can maintain growth without fueling wage inflation.
"There's still a tremendous amount of room for growth in the industry," he said.
